
=================================================================
#42 Seung (承)  (647 January)
Arc: The Chunchu Era · place: surabol · tone: political thriller — countdown
Logline: Five nights of tea between the camps, and a score still tied. On the fifth, Bidam asks the one question Yushin has never answered in Surabol.
=================================================================
[0] ══ DAY: DAY 2 ══
[1] ¶ Of course he comes. Yushin has never once refused Bidam a rematch. Between the camps a small pavilion goes up, open on every side, so nobody can say the other side hid archers. A low table. Tea already poured. A half moon in an empty sky. They meet the way they used to after sparring: gloves off, courtesy on.
[2] Bidam: Yushin. / Tea first. / …When the Six Elders raised Surabol — Lee, Choi, Jeong, Son, Bae, Seol. / Park came from an egg. / There was no Kim.
[3] Kim Yushin: …And?
[4] Bidam: And now the two Kim houses inside this wall — / Surabol Kim, Alji Kim — / both imports. / I alone… am Six-Elder blood.
[5] ¶ The tea cools between them. Neither man drinks enough to call it peace. Bidam smiles as if nothing ugly had been said — the same smile he wore when he crowned a woman king. Yushin sets his cup down unfinished.
[6] Bidam: Alchun sends his regards. From the middle of the field. / He’s eating alone again.
[7] Kim Yushin: He always did eat between us.
[8] ¶ Three Hwarang. One princess. The yard remembers what the Council never wrote down.
[9] ▼ FLASHBACK 615 The cleverest of the three
    [9.0] ¶ Bidam, Alchun, and Yushin — same Hwarang line, same bruised knuckles, same impossible orbit around **Princess Dukman**. They do not say the word love. The gyuku field says it for them, badly.
    [9.1] Bidam: If the Sacred Bone runs out of men, pick the cleverest woman. / I have known Dukman since we were children. Cleverness is not a gender.
    [9.2] Kim Yushin: Well stood. / Tomorrow on the yard — the hundred-and-ninth is mine.
    [9.3] Alchun: You two will kill each other over a score. / I will kill myself over the girl in the middle. / …That was a joke. File it as a joke.
    [9.4] Queen Sunduk: If you three are finished deciding my life— / the ball is still on the field.
    [9.5] ¶ Even their names take sides. Bidam’s sounds like this soil and its sutras. Chunchu’s is a foreign classic. Any clerk across the sea could file it without asking. Nobody notices yet. Names are patient.
    [9.6] Bidam: Yushin. / Alchun. / If either of you ever makes her cry for a small reason — I will even the score on your face.
[9] ▲ end flashback
[10] ══ DAY: DAY 3 ══
[11] ¶ Arrows trade; messengers lie; the Harmony Council discovers it can convene without deciding anything, which is its highest form. Chunchu’s clerks call the unanimity rule quaint. Bidam calls it ours. Inside the palace, the stewards count eight days of grain.
[12] [battle]
[13] ¶ **Third night.** Same pavilion. Same half moon. Bidam has brought a map — not of the siege, of the roads west.
[14] Bidam: Samhan is being colonized — in blood, and in the mind. / Tang sends institutions. India sends… / …through Queen Heo’s blood, sutras. / Yushin — your eyes are handsome. They are a western colour. / …When I stood first, they called me the liberal.
[15] Kim Yushin: Gaya blood came from the west too. / I… stood up. / Fifteen winters past, when you spoke — you told me to stand.
[16] Bidam: That was when you were weak. / …A joke. Drink your tea.
[17] ¶ On the wall Bidam looks west and remembers a cleaner war — Jade Gate Valley, when the enemy still had the courtesy to be foreign.
[18] ▼ FLASHBACK 636 Jade Gate Valley · 옥문곡
    [18.0] ¶ Baekje sends five hundred armoured men to slip through a valley in the dark and bite a fortress from behind. In midwinter the toads in the palace pond start croaking, which toads do not do. The queen listens for one night. Then she sends steel instead of prayers.
    [18.1] Alchun: Bidam — left ridge. I take the dry creek. / If their captain loosens a saddle, we do not wait for a committee.
    [18.2] Bidam: Finally — an enemy I am allowed to hate in public. / Alchun. On my mark.
    [18.3] ¶ They fall on the Baekje camp at dusk. Their captain climbs a boulder and empties a quiver; the quiver ends before the argument does. Alchun takes the general. Bidam takes the valley’s silence.
    [18.4] Alchun: We make a good pair when the target is outside the wall. / Inside the wall… we will see.
    [18.5] Bidam: Inside the wall is still the sacred country. / I do not miss.
    [18.6] ¶ Eleven years later, on Radiance’s rampart, Bidam will remember the Jade Gate as the last time Alchun stood on his side without hesitating.
[18] ▲ end flashback
[19] ¶ Before the fourth night’s tea, the Moon Palace tries a quieter weapon. Chunchu sends his son **Bupmin**, twenty-one, to the steam — the water that shows a man’s inner conscience, the past that is driving his hand. Yushin is told only to **keep him talking**.
[20] ¶ Chunchu is home from the islands. They kept him just long enough to be rude about it, then sent him back with compliments and no ships.
[21] King Muyeol: Bupmin. / Take a jar. / The spring is a place your uncle knows. You’re a Kim — the door will open. / Splash him.
[22] King Munmu: Father… / What does the water do to a man… / I understand. I’ll go.
[23] ── SCENE: The Steam Cavern ──
[24] ¶ This is the first time the cavern goddesses meet Bupmin. He is twenty-one. He does not yet have a king’s name. He has a jar and Chunchu’s weather.
[25] Narim: A Kim. / Sit. No — the jar first. / You… He is the best of both. Gaya in the shoulders. Surabol in the mouth. Golhwa is going to climb you if you stay standing. Sit.
[26] Golhwa: Oh. / A Kim we haven’t had. He’s both. / Take the water. Conscience sticks to it. Trauma. Grudge. Whatever’s driving the hand. / …And stop standing like that.
[27] Golhwa: I’m trying to be a hill and you are shaped like a problem I want in my lap.
[28] Hyullé: …Be careful. / If you splash it, you see why he’s doing it. / If you don’t see anything… that’s its own answer. / …He’s pretty. I’ll be quiet. I won’t be calm.
[29] King Munmu: Goddesses… / Thank you. I was only— / I’ll just take the water.
[30] ¶ He fills the jar. He does not stay for the lake’s other lessons. He is the best of both, and he leaves because his father told him to.
[31] ══ DAY: DAY 4 ══
[32] ¶ Seven days of grain. The Moon Palace’s wells drop. Rumour rises to replace them. Chunchu files contingency letters the way other men file prayers.
[33] ¶ Fourth night. Same low table under the half moon. Bidam reads a rumoured draft — never enough secretariat, never enough emperor. His voice stays pleasant. The sentences do not.
[34] Bidam: What Chunchu wants… / is a country that fits inside a Tang envelope. / Central rule. Emperor. Clerks. / He would burn the Harmony Council’s unanimity — the one thing we kept.
[35] Kim Yushin: Baekje comes with swords, not sentences.
[36] Bidam: Yes — and that is why you always win. / On the yard, and here. / Effort… speaks louder than my blood. / …The year they crowned her, I was the liberal who stood for the woman king. / Now they call me the blood-and-soil man. Ironic, Yushin?
[37] Kim Yushin: …That young Hwarang is still here.
[38] Bidam: Where?
[39] ¶ He folds the rumoured draft. The next sentences have been waiting in the sleeve all night.
[40] Bidam: Princess Seungman, and the tyranny of Kim Chunchu — I stand against both. / He speaks of a thousand-year kingdom. / If his faction wins, Samhan will spend those thousand years as a Chinese vassal. / A country that never again turns its own wheel.
[41] Kim Yushin: Under Seungman, with these reforms, Silla could be the strongest country in Samhan in a few harvests.
[42] Bidam: I do not need the strongest nation. / I want neighbours who still know one another’s names. / The young lifting the old. / A true people — not strangers who happen to share a wall.
[43] Kim Yushin: The people’s livelihood hangs on the nation’s fullness. / Fullness hangs on institutions — on a government that can still stand. / If Silla falls behind Baekje and Goryeo, what comes through the pass is spear and famine. / Then tell me how the neighbours keep their names.
[44] Bidam: Yushin. / Has the royal house spent one year outside the capital? Has Chunchu? / I have. / Out there, nobody wants a foreign emperor’s yoke.
[45] Kim Yushin: As for outsiders, Lord Bidam, I will always be more outsider than you. / You, of Six-Elder blood, speak poorly of the halls that raised this land, / while I, last son of a conquered kingdom, would die for it.
[46] ¶ Yushin does not close the argument. He asks again about the pass, about names, about harvests — anything that keeps Bidam’s back to the dark. Behind the pavilion, Bupmin’s jar ticks once against a post.
[47] Kim Yushin: Bidam. / Say it once more. / The people have no wish for an emperor. Where did you hear that?
[48] ¶ Bupmin comes from behind to **splash the water**. It is ugly and precise — cavern water as a hard sheet across Bidam’s shoulders, beads and all.
[49] Bidam: Ha… / What is this…
[50] King Munmu: Your trauma…. / Yushin… why isn’t it doing anything…?
[51] ¶ Nothing rises. No childhood. No princess. No grudge-film in the steam. The water runs off the black robe as if it had mistaken a man for a wound. Chunchu, at the pavilion’s edge, does not move. The stoic act holds; the eyes do not.
[52] King Muyeol: ……
[53] Bidam: Oh… haha… / I’ve heard of this… this is that water, isn’t it…?
[54] Bidam: HAHAHAHAHA!
[55] Bidam: Behold, the arrogance of the sacred bone class!! / You really thought I had to have some sort of personal trauma?? / That that was the reason I was doing all of this? / That I hated the princess? The queen? / That I hated you, Chunchu, or Yushin? / Have you ever… even for a SECOND… considered the POSSIBILITY… / that your ideas are simply terrible? / That they’ll lead this nation to ruin? / That ANY reasonable man would oppose them? / Or are you so ARROGANT to assume… that EVERYTHING you lot do is correct… / and that the ONLY reason for ANYONE to disagree… is because they were suffering some sort of mental disease? Because they were angry and bitter? / Ha… well, my friends, I’m afraid all you’ve done tonight is prove your point. / You’ve proven yourself to be unworthy of leading any country. / So please… my friends… step aside…!
[56] ¶ Alchun, arriving late with a lamp, goes pale. An officer asks whether to seize the jar. Nobody answers. Bidam is still laughing, and still alive, and the beads are still counting.
[57] ── SCENE: Chunchu’s Rooms ──
[58] King Muyeol: If Bidam wins, the Secretariat becomes a quaint hobby. / If Bidam loses, we still have a dying queen and a Tang-shaped hole in the west. / The man would burn a good idea for arriving in a Tang envelope. That is the whole platform — and it polls well. / Munhee — pack for either weather.
[59] Munhee: I already packed. / I packed the year the Queen was crowned. You only notice in sieges.
[60] ¶ Alchun eats alone between the camps. Both sides send him wine. He drinks neither. Surabol will later call it treason with better stationery.
[61] ══ DAY: DAY 5 ══
[62] ¶ Fifth night — the pavilion again. They sit on the floor, alone, the way they used to meet on the training ground. The tea is cold before anyone raises a blade. Six days of grain.
[63] Kim Yushin: Second Blade of Samhan — Bidam!! Lay down your arms and give your loyalty back to the Blue Moon!!
[64] ¶ For a breath they are only the old score again — one hundred and eight to one hundred and eight — two boys who never let the other keep a lead. Then Bidam speaks, and the yard is gone.
[65] ▼ FLASHBACK 618 One hundred and eight
    [65.0] ¶ The yard after rain. Two Hwarang, neither willing to leave the mud with the score uneven.
    [65.1] Bidam: One hundred and eight…! / Today I take the lead, Gaya!
    [65.2] Kim Yushin: One hundred and eight. / Get up, hyung. An uneven number does not sleep.
    [65.3] Bidam: Ha! / Afraid it will be written that Gaya blood lost to Silla blood?
    [65.4] Kim Yushin: Written or not. / Again.
    [65.5] Bidam: …And don’t call me hyung when you’re winning.
    [65.6] ¶ They end the evening even. They always do.
[65] ▲ end flashback
[66] Bidam: Yushin. / In this country the smartest people hate this country, / and the most patriotic people… are all stupid. / That’s Silla. / The country you’re trying to sell.
[67] Bidam: Yushin…. / And besides — you… / **you were never even of Silla…!**
[68] Bidam: Blood is inevitable.
[69] ¶ The tea has not been touched. He says it like a compliment that curdled — still the gentleman, still the black robe, still the voice that once shielded this same man from the yard.
[70] Kim Yushin: Lord Bidam… I remember we swore our lives to this together…
[71] Bidam: You never had a country of your own — selling this one must cost you nothing… / But we are different. We cannot be cut from this land… / Would you hand the country my ancestors built to an emperor…! / I am a son of the sacred country.
[72] Kim Yushin: Selling — I have sold nothing. / Lord Chunchu only asks that we learn Tang’s institutions. Baekje comes with swords, not sentences.
[73] Bidam: Chunchu — 春秋. The man is named after a Chinese book. / And you would let him write the sacred country’s tomorrow. / Learn another country’s institutions long enough — and one morning, the learning is all that is left.
[74] Bidam: I will raise the sacred country’s glory again, / I will return the sacred country’s future to its own people!
[75] ¶ Yushin does not answer the speech. He looks at the cold tea as if the answer were at the bottom of the cup.
[76] Bidam: Yumjong says your great-grandfather drove Geumgwan to Surabol in a cart. / Fine. Everyone knows the cart. / Nobody talks about the grandfather. What did he hand over, Yushin?
[77] Kim Yushin: Leave the dead in their rooms, Bidam.
[78] Bidam: No. / Five nights you’ve drunk my tea and told me nothing that was yours. / Give me one thing. Then call me a traitor.
[79] ¶ For a long time the only sound is the wind through the open pavilion. Yushin has not said this aloud in Surabol since he was fifteen.
[80] Kim Yushin: …Baekje has a name for one night on the Gwansan road. / Ask any soldier over the western hills. They call it the Severing.
[81] Bidam: The night their king lost his head. Everyone knows it. A slave held the knife.
[82] Kim Yushin: A slave held the knife. / A man in a Gaya cone helm sat their king on a camp stool and told him to sit. / …That was my grandfather.
[83] ¶ Bidam’s beads stop for the second time this winter.
[84] Bidam: …A Gaya prince broke the oldest peace in Samhan. / For us.
[85] Kim Yushin: For Silla. / And his grandson sits at your table and hears he was never of it.
[86] Bidam: …Drink your tea, Marshal.
[87] ¶ Neither of them drinks. Bidam does not ask the grandfather’s name, and Yushin does not offer it. Some names a family keeps in a box.
[88] ¶ **A cone helm, a king on a camp stool, and a name Yushin won’t say. Who was his grandfather…?**
